data.body: # PuPu 0.1.13 — Smoother conversations, more reliable memory Stop and retry conversations with less friction, restore background memory learning, and repair the Windows update configuration as we prepare for Agent Builder. > **Windows users: install 0.1.13 manually once if your current app cannot check for updates.** Earlier affected installations, including the inspected public 0.1.12 Windows package, are missing the updater configuration and cannot repair themselves through automatic update. The installer below includes the fix, enabling those installations to receive future compatible releases through the app. Your existing chats and settings should be retained; back up important data before upgrading. ([#409](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/409)) ## Download PuPu 0.1.13 ### Windows [![Download for Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-Windows_x64-0078D4?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.13/PuPu-0.1.13-windows-x64-setup.exe) ### macOS [![Download for Mac — Apple Silicon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mac-Apple_Silicon-111827?style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.13/PuPu-0.1.13-macos-arm64.dmg) [![Download for Mac — Intel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mac-Intel-64748B?style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.13/PuPu-0.1.13-macos-x64.dmg) Not sure which Mac you have? Open **Apple menu → About This Mac**. Choose **Apple Silicon** for an Apple M-series chip, or **Intel** for an Intel processor. ### Linux [![Download for Ubuntu / Debian x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ubuntu_%2F_Debian-x64_DEB-E95420?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.13/PuPu-0.1.13-linux-x64.deb) [![Download Linux AppImage x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-x64_AppImage-2563EB?style=for-the-badge&logo=linux&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.13/PuPu-0.1.13-linux-x64.AppImage) ## What's improved ### Stop, edit and try again without getting stuck Stopping a run restores the composer promptly while background cleanup finishes, without removing the visible conversation or tool history. Failed or cancelled attempts now settle more reliably so they do not indefinitely block edits, resends or the next message. ([#389](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/389)) ### Memory learning back on track Fixed memory proposal creation for eligible completed conversations, restoring delivery of valid candidates to the existing background curator. Proposals stay tied to their conversation evidence, with records of whether work was queued or skipped. This does not introduce automatic cross-conversation memory sharing or a new Memory settings interface. ([#401](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/401)) ### Windows updates, repaired in the installer The signed Windows installer now includes the production update-feed configuration. Release checks validate that configuration in the installed package and after a real upgrade-and-restart cycle, so the missing configuration cannot silently pass qualification again. Existing affected Windows installations still need the one-time manual installation described above. ([#409](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/409)) ### Gemini 4 Argon in the model catalog Added native Gemini 4 Argon catalog and model-selection support, including its supported thinking settings, without changing the default Gemini model. Availability depends on provider access and service limits. Live generation, vision and tool-completion verification could not be completed because the provider returned HTTP 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` responses; catalog and request-contract checks are not a claim of successful live generation. ([#411](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/411)) ### Small fixes that make a difference - Improved `/fyi` and `/btw` handling when a supported live channel is still starting. If the active run cannot accept the command, PuPu now explains the queue fallback instead of silently changing its meaning. This is not full live steering for every recipe graph. ([#381](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/381)) - Removed an invisible Skill Organizer click target that could open the organizer while the command palette was closed. ([#399](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/399)) - Hardened release-network retries and the Mac Intel notarization transport to reduce failures caused by transient external-service connections. ([#417](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/pull/417), [#419](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/pull/419), [#420](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/pull/420)) ## Installation and upgrade verification macOS Apple Silicon and Intel packages are signed and notarized. The Windows x64 installer is code-signed. Linux x64 packages are available as AppImage and DEB. The sealed 0.1.13 candidate passed fresh-install qualification on all four platform targets, plus native **0.1.12 → 0.1.13** download, installation and restart qualification on Windows x64 and macOS Apple Silicon/Intel. Those checks also verified installed-package identities and retained user-data sentinels. Upgrade qualification uses signed 0.1.12 test fixtures and a local test feed. It proves the tested native upgrade paths into the exact sealed 0.1.13 packages, **not** that an unmodified Windows 0.1.12 installation with missing updater configuration can discover the update. It also does not cover every older version, user environment or public-network condition. Linux users should install the new package manually. Back up important chats and settings before upgrading. Older app/runtime versions may not understand repaired run-history records, so do not assume downgrading a modified profile is safe. [Candidate verification](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/actions/runs/39734068226) · [Installation and upgrade qualification](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/actions/runs/39811090757) ## 🚧 Agent Builder countdown: next stop, v0.2.0 With 0.1.13, our next planned feature milestone is **v0.2.0 — Agent Builder**. The focus is a usable basic visual builder and the stable runtime it needs: construct agent workflows, understand their execution and see what happens at each step. [Follow the milestone](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/208). Our goal goes beyond an editable node graph tied to PuPu. We want technical and non-technical users alike to build useful agents, validate their behavior and take them into their own software. As part of that direction, we plan to support **exporting agents and workflows as Python projects**—code and resources you can inspect, extend and integrate into your own applications. Build visually in PuPu; keep ownership of what you build. **Build in PuPu. Make it your own.** *This is a roadmap preview, not Agent Builder or Python-project export shipped in 0.1.13. Python export's delivery version and compatibility details remain to be confirmed; this preview is not a guarantee that every roadmap capability will arrive in 0.2.0.* ## Feedback If something goes wrong, please [open an issue](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues) with your operating system, provider/model and reproduction steps. Remove credentials and private conversation content before sharing logs. External model and integration services may require separate accounts, API keys or payments. **[Full changelog: v0.1.12 → v0.1.13](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/compare/v0.1.12...v0.1.13)**

data.body: # PuPu 0.1.12 — Better models, smarter Skills, smoother memory A dedicated home for model setup, Skills that preserve your original messages, and less unnecessary work around conversation memory. ## A major quality and stability update Following broader hands-on testing, PuPu 0.1.12 was rebuilt to address a substantial set of bugs across core product flows and tighten the overall experience before publication. This rebuild improves tool-result delivery and replay, interrupted tool-chain recovery, streamed reasoning presentation, token-usage accounting, Skill inventory consistency, provider retry diagnostics, Gemini model handling, bounded tool-output reads, and the grouping of related tool activity. ([#369](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/369), [#370](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/370), [#371](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/371), [#377](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/377), [#382](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/382), [#383](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/383), [#384](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/384), [#386](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/386), [#390](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/390)) The rebuilt candidate completed fresh end-to-end QA, signed packaging on Windows and macOS, fresh-install qualification on all four supported targets, and restart-update qualification from v0.1.11 on Windows x64 and macOS Apple Silicon/Intel. ## Download PuPu 0.1.12 ### Windows [![Download for Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Download-Windows_x64-0078D4?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.12/PuPu-0.1.12-windows-x64-setup.exe) ### macOS [![Download for Mac — Apple Silicon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mac-Apple_Silicon-111827?style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.12/PuPu-0.1.12-macos-arm64.dmg) [![Download for Mac — Intel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mac-Intel-64748B?style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.12/PuPu-0.1.12-macos-x64.dmg) Not sure which Mac you have? Open **Apple menu → About This Mac**. Choose **Apple Silicon** for an Apple M-series chip, or **Intel** for an Intel processor. ### Linux [![Download for Ubuntu / Debian x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ubuntu_%2F_Debian-x64_DEB-E95420?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.12/PuPu-0.1.12-linux-x64.deb) [![Download Linux AppImage x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-x64_AppImage-2563EB?style=for-the-badge&logo=linux&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/download/v0.1.12/PuPu-0.1.12-linux-x64.AppImage) ## What's new ### A dedicated home for your model providers Open **Models** from the side menu to manage provider API keys and browse, download or remove Ollama models. Closing the page returns you to your chat; choosing a model for a conversation still happens in the composer. Kimi and DeepSeek now display their own identities instead of a generic “Custom” badge. ([#204](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/204), [#347](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/347)) The shipped catalog also gains new OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek API entries while preserving existing model IDs and selections. Availability depends on your provider account. ([#354](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/354)) ### Skills that preserve your words Invoking a Skill no longer expands its instructions into your message. Your request stays intact: Skills are discovered through concise descriptions, with full instructions loaded on activation. Standard `SKILL.md` folders and explicit `/name` invocation share this lifecycle across PuPu and Unchain. ([#291](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/291), [#327](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/327)) ### Less waiting around memory Context preparation reuses verified conversation history and defers older-memory reads until needed. Background memory organization is separated from foreground conversation completion. Clearer activity descriptions and updated Memory settings distinguish the current service from legacy controls. Memory remains **active, not shadow**. ([#349](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/349), [#279](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/279)) ### New writing and research options in the Store - **Document coauthoring:** gather context, draft, revise and test a document with a fresh reader. ([#289](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/289)) - **Humanizer:** edit prose with your selected model—without a separate Humanizer service. It is not an authorship detector or a promise to bypass detection. ([#329](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/329)) - **Zotero:** constrained, read-only access to search a local library and retrieve citation metadata. ([#290](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/290)) These optional third-party integrations have their own requirements and limitations. Store inclusion does not imply full security certification; model-provider usage may incur separate charges. ## Fixes and developer improvements - Improved web-fetch content handling and truncation visibility. ([#226](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/226)) - Improved Ollama reasoning visibility. ([#274](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/274)) - Fixed Kimi K2.7 Code thinking/tool-call replay compatibility for verified warm conversation paths; see the remaining restart limitation below. ([#292](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/292)) - Corrected Test API reporting of streaming, theme and locale state. ([#275](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/275)) - Added clearer contributor guidance for finding, claiming and submitting a first task. ([#315](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/315)) ## Installation and upgrades macOS Apple Silicon and Intel packages are signed and notarized; the Windows x64 installer is code-signed. Linux x64 packages are available as AppImage and DEB. Fresh-install qualification passed on all four targets. Upgrade-and-restart qualification from **0.1.11 to 0.1.12** passed on Windows x64 and macOS Apple Silicon/Intel using the rebuilt sealed release candidate. Linux users should install the new package manually. Other source versions are not covered by this upgrade qualification; back up important chats and settings before upgrading. These results cover the tested installation and upgrade paths, not every provider, plugin or conversation scenario. ## Known limitations - A Kimi tool run paused for approval across an app restart may restore its approval card without continuing execution. Warm tool-call compatibility is improved, but this cold-restart case is not claimed as fixed. ([#292](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues/292)) - Agent Builder, Characters, user-authored custom providers and Computer Use remain disabled in this release's build defaults. Built-in DeepSeek and Kimi remain available. - External services may require separate accounts, API keys or payments. If something goes wrong, please [open an issue](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/issues) with your operating system, provider/model and reproduction steps. Remove credentials and private conversation content before sharing logs. ## 🚧 Agent Builder countdown: build visually, take it with you One planned feature release, **v0.1.13**, stands between this release and **v0.2.0**, our Agent Builder milestone, currently targeted for **November 2026**. But our goal is more than an editable graph of agent nodes. We want technical and non-technical users alike to build useful workflows efficiently—and we don't believe those workflows should be locked inside PuPu. As part of that direction, we plan to support **exporting workflows as Python projects**. Start visually in PuPu, then take your workflow into your own codebase, extend it, and make it part of a future project. The visual builder should be a starting point, not a boundary. **Build in PuPu. Make it your own.** *This is a roadmap preview, not functionality shipped in v0.1.12. November is a target, not a guaranteed release date; the delivery version for Python export is still to be confirmed.* **[Full changelog: v0.1.11 → v0.1.12](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/compare/v0.1.11...v0.1.12)**

data.body: # PuPu 0.1.9 — Early Preview Release 🚀 A desktop AI client with a file-system chat explorer, memory, workspace context, and runtime management for both local and cloud models. ## What's New in 0.1.9 This release is about one idea: **everything you can give the assistant now lives in one place.** Toolkits, MCP servers, and skills used to be separate concepts with separate flows — 0.1.9 folds them into a single Plugin Store, and adds skills as a first-class way to work. - 🧩 **One Plugin Store — toolkits, MCP servers, and skills together** — the old toolkit modal is gone, replaced by a proper in-app store. A **Discover** page opens on a featured pick, curated essentials, and collections that expand inline to show what's inside. A unified sidebar sorts the whole catalog by type — **Toolkits / MCP / Skills** — and every entry gets a real detail page with its README, permissions, and where it came from. Curated picks install in one click, with no credentials to set up first. - ⌨️ **Skills, as slash commands** — this is the big one. Skills declared by any installed plugin appear directly in the `/` menu in the composer. Pick one and it expands inline into a ready-to-edit template, and using it selects that plugin for just that run — nothing to configure, nothing that sticks around afterward. - 📚 **Skill packs — install a whole workflow at once** — browse and install curated skill packs (**Prompt Master**, **Frontend Design**, and more) in one click from the Skills section, or point PuPu at a local folder of `SKILL.md` files to turn your own into a pack. - 🛟 **Long runs that survive a crash** — a long agent run is no longer tied to the life of the app. Interactions are now durable: each execution attempt is recorded and bound to its session, so if the app or the runtime dies mid-run, the work reconnects to the right conversation on restart instead of being lost or duplicated. Pending tool confirmations survive with it. - 🔁 **Steadier long-running execution** — extensive hardening of the run loop itself: execution control, recovery, and the durable job worker were rebuilt so that long, many-tool runs hold up. This release was soak-tested with multi-agent runs driving hundreds of tool calls, and they now complete without a single retried attempt. - ✨ **A real startup experience** — the blank loading window is gone. PuPu now boots through a single themed overlay with one continuous progress bar from the very first frame until the app is ready, over an ambient blurred field derived from your own theme colors. - ⚠️ **Install failures explain themselves** — when an MCP install fails, the actual underlying cause now surfaces on the card and detail panel instead of leaving you at a silent dead end. ### Fixes & Polish - 🧠 **Memory contract hardening** — memory calls now go through a transparent contract proxy, ending a whole class of silent breakage where unrecognized arguments were quietly dropped instead of raising. - 💾 **Sturdier settings storage** — settings moved further onto a transactional local database: resetting is a single atomic operation, pending writes are drained on quit so nothing is lost on exit, and the storage page groups everything by category. - 🖌️ **Consistent surfaces everywhere** — dropdowns, segmented controls, switches, menus, chips, and code/diff blocks were swept onto shared sizing, radius, and border rules, so the same control looks the same in every modal — and light/dark parity is noticeably tighter. - 💬 **Composer fixes** — the empty-state greeting no longer overlaps the floating attach panel, dropdown options stop compressing when a list scrolls, and dropdown scrolling no longer chains into the panel behind it. - 🌍 **Translation sweep** — all 11 shipped languages were filled in for the new plugins and skills surfaces. - 🧪 **Release quality** — fixes across the release QA pipeline, end-to-end credential handling, and web build warnings so the release gate runs clean. ## ⚠️ Known Limitations This is still an **early preview**. Some features are incomplete and edge-case bugs may still exist. If you hit one, please open an issue. --- ## On the Horizon Following the v0.1.5 convention, a short forward-looking note — roadmap previews, not release commitments. Scope and timing may change. - **Custom model providers** — bring your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with its own base URL and key, and have its models flow through the catalog and model picker like any built-in provider. Landing behind the scenes now. - **Computer use** — letting PuPu see the screen and drive the mouse and keyboard, gated behind explicit consent and per-model support. In active development; not yet enabled. - **Agent Builder** — a visual way to define a reusable agent's prompt, model defaults, and tool access, then call that agent directly from chat for repeatable workflows.

Type `/` in the composer during streaming to see them. - 🗂️ **Redesigned input & attach panel** — the composer got a rebuilt attach panel: cleaner toolkit / workspace / model controls, a tidier attachment chip row, and a compact queue pile that shows what's lined up next — all keyboard-reachable. - 🧭 **New chat minimap** — the message-window minimap was rebuilt around evenly-spaced semantic markers, so navigating long conversations is smoother and stays responsive even during streaming. - 💾 **Faster, more reliable chat storage** — conversations now live in a local database instead of being rewritten wholesale on every change. Large libraries stay snappy, and history is more durable. - 📦 **Tools that just install — local runtime auto-setup** — MCP servers that need **Node (npx)** or **UV (uvx)** now get their runtime resolved and set up automatically. No more installs that silently fail because the environment wasn't ready. - ⚠️ **Clear install errors** — when a toolkit install does fail, you now see the actual reason right on the toolkit card and detail panel, instead of a silent dead end. ### Fixes & Polish - ⚡ **Smoother streaming** — reduced high-frequency re-renders while a response streams: persistence writes are throttled and deduplicated, the trace-chain timeline no longer rebuilds on every chunk, and the minimap runs mostly imperatively so it stays fluid. - 🔗 **Trace chain finality** — fixed trace-chain completion ownership so tool/reasoning frames close out reliably, and fixed duplicate live text in no-tool turns (#155, #66). - 🧭 **Smarter scrolling** — landing correction and scroll navigation for the message window, compensation for boot-window expansion and large streamed chunks, plus a bottom-viewport inset so the last message and the minimap aren't clipped. - 🗂️ **Steadier Explorer** — collapsed folders no longer flash open during drag-and-drop, and collapsed folders unmount lazily to keep large trees light. - 🎨 **Semantic theming under the hood** — shell, input, context menu, card, modal, and markdown think-block backgrounds are all routed through semantic tokens for cleaner light/dark parity. - 🛠️ **Steadier runtime** — hardened the Unchain sidecar: safer interject setup and teardown, no catalog reads while Unchain is still starting, and fixes to the PuPu MCP store install / OAuth flows and build hooks. ## ⚠️ Known Limitations This is still an **early preview**. This is where the subagent-pool idea above becomes something you can build you

Fixed **duplicate / nested chat IDs** in subagent runs. - **Compact context menu** for a tidier right-click experience. ## The PuPu Experience The capabilities that make up everyday PuPu — refined, not reinvented, this release - 💬 **Chat & streaming** — real-time responses, a trace timeline for tool calls, astable long-chat performanc - 📎 **Attachments** — drag-and-drop images and PDFs with local storage and clean in-chat display. - 🧠 **Memory** — short-term context within a chat, long-term recall across chats, plus Memory Inspect and set - 🗂️ **Workspace-aware chat** — manage multiple workspaces and select the right oneper chat to keep answers gr - 🛠️ **Tools & execution** — tools integrated into the chat flow, terminal vs. fileoperations cleanly separateo prevent accidental runs. - 🤖 **Model providers** — manage OpenAI/Anthropic keys in-app, browse and one-click-pull Ollama model. - 💾 **Storage & runtime** — inspect storage usage, manage localStorage and Ollama models, and clean up runtim - 🎨 **Desktop experience** — a native workflow across local and hosted models, with in-app updates and a more c ## ⚠️ Known Limitations This is still an **early preview**. Some features are incomplete, and edge-case bugs may still exist. If you hit --- ## Why We're Building PuPu PuPu started from a simple belief: the best way to improve a tool is to keep exploring how people actually use it. When we looked at how chat apps like ChatGPT and Claude organize conversations, we noticed something missing — there was no real way to *file* your chats. So we built a **file-system-style explorer**, where conversations live in folders you control, the way you'd organize anything else that matters. When we watched people read long model responses, we saw them lose their place while scrolling. So we added a **minimap-style scroll bar** — a bird's-eye view of an entire answer and a faster way to move through it. But improving on what already exists was never the whole goal. While we keep pace with the mainstream AI platforms, we also want to follow our own ideas about what a desktop AI client *could* be: - **We want the AI to fully drive the UI** — not just generate text inside a fixed layout, but actually shape what the app shows you. - **We want a genuinely new way to build agents.** Today, almost every "agent builder" is a workflow — boxes and arrows wired together by hand. We don't believe a truly capable agent, one that can handle most of what you throw at it, should be a workflow at all. So we're proposing a **subagent pool**: you define a set of agents, and a main agent freely orchestrates them as each situation demands — no rigid graph, no pre-drawn path. We know this road is hard, and there's a lot still ahead of us. If any of this resonates with you, we'd love for you to **join us** — and if you're already using PuPu, please **tell us what you think**. data.body: # PuPu 0.1.6 - Early Preview Release 🚀 v0.1 is a major upgrade focused on chat workflow, architecture cleanup, and product polish. ## Major Functionality PuPu is a desktop AI client built for everyday work with both local and cloud models. It combines chat, tools, memory, workspace context, and runtime management in one streamlined app. - 💬 **Chat and streaming** - Real-time streaming responses with improved visibility during generation. - Trace timeline support for following tool calls and execution flow more clearly. - Better resend flow and more stable long-chat performance. - 📎 **Attachments and input workflow** - Drag-and-drop support for images and PDFs. - Local attachment storage and cleaner attachment display in chat. - Refined chat input and attach panel experience for faster everyday use. - 🧠 **Memory system** - Short-term memory keeps recent conversation context available during a chat. - Long-term memory helps retain reusable facts, preferences, and workflows across chats. - Built-in Memory Inspect and configurable memory settings for better control and visibility. - 🗂️ **Workspace-aware chat** - Add and manage multiple workspaces. - Select workspaces per chat to keep conversations grounded in the right files and folders. - Workspace validation and runtime directory support for a more reliable local workflow. - 🛠️ **Tools and execution** - Tool usage is integrated directly into the chat workflow. - Terminal and workspace-related capabilities are separated more clearly, with workspace actions focused on file-based operations. - Confirmation flow helps prevent accidental tool execution. - 🤖 **Model provider management** - Manage OpenAI and Anthropic API keys directly inside the app. - Browse Ollama models by category, search quickly, and inspect model metadata. - Pull local models with one click, track download progress, and monitor active downloads in real time. - 💾 **Local storage and runtime management** - Inspect app storage usage and manage localStorage entries safely. - Check Ollama status, review installed models, and remove local models when needed. - Inspect runtime file usage under the configured workspace and clean up files when necessary. - 🎨 **Desktop experience** - Native desktop workflow across local models, hosted providers, chat history, settings, and tools. - Updated loading experience, polished UI details, and a more consistent visual system. - In-app update support for faster upgrades. ### New Features in v0.1.6 - Plan toolkit and Git toolkit added ## ⚠️ Known Limitations & Notes - Early Preview Reminder: This is still an early preview release. Some features are incomplete, and edge-case bugs may still exist. ## Bug Fixes - Fix problem: no error message when API key is revoked or expired - approve once, always approve, reject buttons display bugs If you encounter any issues or have suggestions, feel free to report them! 🚀 ## What to expect Starting with upcoming releases, PuPu release notes will include a short forward-looking section. The goal is to keep users and watchers aware of the project direction while keeping shipped changes and future work clearly separated. - **Agent Builder** — PuPu is moving toward a visual builder for reusable agents. The direction is to let users define an agent's prompt, model defaults, tool access, and sub-agent pool, then select that agent directly from chat for repeatable workflows. These are roadmap previews, not release commitments. Scope and timing may change as the features are tested in real workflows.

docs: drop the Discussions channel from the contributor path

Discussions was added as the optional expression-of-interest channel, but an
inbox nobody intends to watch is worse than no inbox: an unanswered thread
reads as an inactive project.

Interest now arrives as a comment on the issue itself, which is where claiming
already happens, so a task keeps one canonical home and no second surface needs
watching. Questions about a task go on that task. Setup problems and unsure
ideas open an issue.

Removes both Discussions contact links, leaving three guide links on the issue
chooser, and removes the Discussions references from README, CONTRIBUTING, and
the first-contribution guide.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: add an onboarding path for external contributors

Newcomers had no starting point: the README presented the MCP store as the
only way in, nothing defined `good first issue` or `help wanted`, no rule said
how a task is claimed, and there was no channel for "I'd like to help".

Add docs/contributing/first-contribution.md as the single page all entry points
lead to, covering contribution types, finding and claiming a task, setup, the
base: dev submission flow, and what a contributor explicitly does not need
(write access, label permissions, board access).

Document the claiming rule identically there and in CONTRIBUTING.md: comment to
claim, a maintainer assigns, 14 days without visible progress releases it.

Route interest and questions to Discussions from the issue-creation screen
rather than onto the issue tracker, matching the convention in comparable
projects. Add CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1).

Repair the README anchor to CONTRIBUTING.md, dead since that heading was
renamed to "Contribute an MCP server, Skill, or Toolkit".

Closes #315
